title: Where the Ceiling of the Amount at Risk Bites in a Dispute Rebill
content:
Where the ceiling of the amount at risk bites, and whether the interest relief is deducted before or after it, turns on the money the cardholder moves through Personal Checking and on whether Personal Checking has charged the cardholder a fee. This governs rebills on cards under Personal Credit Cards.

*Where Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts in the last six months total at least 12000.00 USD and no Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the interest relief is deducted from the product of the rebilled share first and the ceiling of the amount at risk is compared with the figure that results.

*Where those deposits total at least 12000.00 USD and at least one Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the ceiling of the amount at risk is compared with the product of the rebilled share before any relief is deducted, and the interest relief is then deducted from the capped figure.

*Where those deposits total less than 12000.00 USD* — the rebilled share acts on the amount at risk with no interest relief deducted and the ceiling of the amount at risk is compared with the product.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** Take an amount at risk of 640.00 USD, a product of the rebilled share of 576.00 USD and an interest relief of 41.50 USD. Under the first convention the relief is taken from 576.00 USD, giving 534.50 USD, and the lesser of 534.50 USD and 640.00 USD is 534.50 USD. Under the second the lesser of 576.00 USD and 640.00 USD is 576.00 USD, from which the relief is then taken, giving 534.50 USD. Under the third the relief is not taken at all and the figure is 576.00 USD.

**On the boundaries.** The deposit figure is read as at least, so deposits of exactly 12000.00 USD in the last six months belong with the higher band and 11999.00 USD with the lower, where the count of checking fees does not come into it.
